analysis:
Examined all supplied units, including unchanged lifecycle context, ProviderLoop state, the bounded patches and unchanged file modes. ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift:155 adds awaited cluster-update drain processing to the existing lifecycle mailbox monitor. ProviderLoop.swift:566-569 adds an optional request ID and task to retain ownership of that drain; those declarations alone do not change serving permissions. Existing lifecycle code closes admission (Lifecycle.swift:15-16), counts accepted/local requests (19-22), distinguishes forced cancellation from graceful completion, and requires native-owner retirement and coordinator settlement before reporting graceful success (84-125). No supplied change alters encryption, cache isolation/persistence, keys, billing messages or App Attest authorization checks; no concrete regression is established here.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain and its mailbox/supervisor implementations: validate target/process identity and cluster-member restriction, bounded/nonblocking file reads, replay handling, admission ownership and release, task cancellation, and coexistence with lifecycle/model-switch/add-on drains. Because the new handler is awaited in the shared monitor, confirm that it launches long-running drain work rather than waiting for completion and delaying later stop/add-on commands (Lifecycle.swift:147-156). Relevant contracts are A-018, TB-012, T-059/T-060 and T-043; connection/worker transitions must preserve TB-011 and T-053. These implementations are outside the supplied source, so their absence is a coverage limit, not evidence of missing controls. The canonical index and selected T-041 detail were considered; no cache-related change appears in this scope.
